People ask: “Are you dunking on neolabs?”

Most neolabs will fail. That’s normal. But I believe more AI breakthroughs are coming.

I’m skeptical of those following the same playbook as OpenAI and Anthropic. Raising $1B and spending 50% on GPUs doesn’t make you a $10B company.

I’m rooting for the contrarians. Challenge scaling laws. Challenge transformers. Challenge how models learn. Challenge the next-token prediction paradigm.

My bigger concern is that brilliant researchers don’t necessarily make great founders. In my experience, researchers often struggle to turn their research into great products / sustainable businesses.

2003 年 3 月 10 日，美国加州帕萨迪纳市议会开特别会议。帕萨迪纳在洛杉矶旁边，是加州理工学院所在的城市。公众发言环节，一个穿灰 T 恤的大学生走到话筒前：

“我叫 Dario Amodei，是加州理工学院的大二学生。”

他带来一份反对伊拉克战争的请愿书。上周四递交时，有 400 名加州理工师生签名，到这天已经接近 600 人。他当场把请愿书念了一遍，其中一句是：

“我们创造推动这个国家前进的技术，看到它被不加区分地用于战争，深感痛心。”

发言最后，他说：“请不要扼杀和平而激动人心的科学——它为这座城市带来就业，为全人类带来进步。”

10 天后，伊拉克战争爆发。18 年后，他和几位前 OpenAI 同事联合创办了 Anthropic。

20 岁时他担心的，是自己这代人做出的技术被拿去打仗。现在他整天担心的是 AI 被利用。

这段 2 分钟的发言出自帕萨迪纳市政府存档的会议录像，我加了中英双语字幕，可以对照着看。

线索：X 用户 @dummerspast39
原始录像：https://pasadena.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?view_id=25（2003 年 3 月 10 日市议会特别会议）

我其实是比较相信Peter Thiel所说的技术大停滞的。中国人可能感受不深，因为在改开之前中国的基线足够的低，这几十年下来光靠引入外部技术就已经感受颇深了。但是实际上，在西方，原子世界基本上没有什么变化，唯一有大进步的只有计算机。国内现在也能感受到了，生化环材四大天坑的根本原因就是在这儿。这几个专业非常重要，但是技术进步太慢，没有办法产业化落地，根本容纳不了就业。

但是整个社会都像是坐在一个坏掉的火车上摇晃身体，假装他前进。大学越来越富丽堂皇，但是里面的学者越来越像是爱因斯坦所说的：
“我尊重这种人，但不能容忍这样的科学家，他们拿出一块木板来，寻找最薄的地方，然后在容易钻透的地方拼命钻许多孔。”
帽子，论文，CNS，一区，二区，科学已经不再是好奇和探索了，人们沉迷于画一个圈，划一个势力范围，当这个王国的里的国王。变成了权力的游戏。
社科，文史哲更是严重，早就堕落了，一帮人互相捧臭脚。这几年更甚，社科的研究方法没啥本质的进步，又要创新，就搞出来一堆乱七八糟的东西，反而给整个社会造成了更多的混乱和灾难。
所有人都心知肚明这些问题，但是没有人能改，这个系统已经是百万漕工衣食所系，不断的加强。大学越来越多的功能是筛选，贴一个牌子，但是教育的功能越来越差。成本越来越高，产出越来越低。
但是大学只是整个社会里面问题最小的一个，政府，法院，各种各样的部门。所有这些都是不断的自我加强，无法改革。AI就像是皇帝的新衣里面的小孩，一下子釜底抽薪，把这些系统赖以生存的地基抽走了。他们维持的假象幻灭了。但是在动荡中，不破不立，有能力的人不再怕老资历，学阀的压制，能够做出难以想象的成果，而那些滥竽充数的混子，也会被一棒子打下去。
混乱不是深渊，混乱是阶梯。

text:
Tony Xu of @DoorDash on getting rejected by investors, competing against rivals with thousands of times more capital, and how founders can tell conviction from delusion:

"I had over 100 rejections in a span of over 1,000 days where the company almost constantly ran out of money... I couldn't raise a dime, and we were running out of capital."

"Companies like Amazon or Uber were in the space who had way more capital than we had. Hundreds of times, maybe thousands of times of capital deployed versus the amount that we raised. So then the question becomes, well, how are you gonna win this cash-burning machine?"

"This is where you as the founder have to finely tune that line between delusion and knowing that you have something that others don't understand. What are the customers telling you?"

"We the founders did deliveries for almost virtually every day the first three years of the company's life... And so we had strong points of view on each side of our marketplace that could explain what was happening in the numbers."

"When you have one set of facts, which is your customers, you have another set of facts, what are called opinions and perceptions, you gotta trust the facts. That's ultimately what kept us going."

As someone with a portfolio of energized land assets here is what I am seeing:

1. Neoclouds are disorganized and poorly capitalized. Some are definitely better than others however. 

2. Hyperscalers are intractable, bureaucratic organizations that take 3 months to do an NDA and want 18mo escrow periods. We built our portfolio by competing against these terms because of our speed and simplicity. The more future assets orgs like ours win, the bigger the problem for the hyperscalers downstream (see 3). 

3. There are delays in the existing pipeline that will catch people off guard in 2027. Hyperacalers will (obviously) react by focusing on their own internal compute needs over any third party. If the third party is a model company, they will tell them to go through their model router where they will also take a non-trivial vig. Them telling Ant they have no compute for them (rumored in Ant’s S-1) if true is a huge tell that this is already happening. 

All of this is to say that it does look like there will be a lot of partially stranded compute and compute sitting in inventory in 2027 than is currently forecasted. This is bought and paid for but effectively underearning (below total cost of capital) or collecting dust. We see this as true for everyone - model companies, hyperscalers, neoclouds except ONE (you can guess which one). 

This dislocation will benefit two kinds of orgs: the non-bureaucratic big scalers who can build industrial scale quickly and the nimble, well capitalized players feeding them. 

2027 will be a turbulent year because it will clear out a bunch of wrong/bad bets. It will also be a consolidation year for a few.

text:
If you've ever wondered why smart TVs are so cheap, this is why.

@log4j rooted his Samsung and found an always-on hot mic, automatic content recognition, geolocation, network mapping, ad targeting and user profiling, shared with Samsung's "400 partners".

A lot of it can be blocked in <15 min, wrote a basic guide below.

What your TV is doing

The main culprit is ACR (automatic content recognition). Your TV screenshots what's on screen, fingerprints it, and sends it home to build your ad profile. Samsung does it every 500ms, LG every 10ms [1].

What is insane: it happens on connected devices too.
Plug in your laptop, your console, your work machine, and your TV can fingerprint that via HDMI [1].
He also found that if your Samsung doesn't have a mic, it'll look for one from a connected soundbar or bluetooth device.
https://x.com/log4j/status/2113762242327892456?s=20
It's on by default, and you likely agreed to it on the setup screen you clicked through in 10 seconds.

Step 1: Turn off ACR

Samsung: Terms & Privacy → Viewing Information Services
LG: Live Plus
Vizio: Viewing Data
Roku: "Use info from TV inputs"
Sony/Google TV: Samba Interactive TV

Menus vary by model, but those are the names to look for. While you're in there, opt out of interest-based ads, reset your advertising ID, decline every optional privacy agreement, turn off voice recognition, and delete apps you never open.

Step 2: Give smart devices their own network

Put the TV, cameras, speakers and vacuum on your router's guest/IoT network. The logic is simple: these devices rarely get patched. If one gets compromised (getting drastically more frequent with AI), it shouldn't be able to see your other devices or home network.

Step 3: Block trackers for the whole house with DNS-level filtering

NextDNS (cloud-based) is easy and has a solid free plan. Pi-hole is a little bit more work if you prefer self hosting. For simplicity we'll focus on the former.

1. Sign up at http://nextdns.io (free tier is plenty)
2. Privacy tab: add a blocklist (OISD is a good bet) and turn on Native Tracking Protection for Samsung, LG, Roku, Amazon (see attached image)
3. Setup tab: copy your endpoint
4. Paste it into your router's DNS settings as DNS-over-HTTPS/TLS (or use the IPs + "Link IP" if your router only does plain DNS)
5. Bonus: block outbound port 53 except to your router. Some devices hardcode their own DNS to get around you

Then open the NextDNS logs and watch how often your TV phones home. It's eye-opening. If an app or update breaks, find the domain in the logs and allowlist it.

Why they do this

TV prices are down 97% since 2000 [2]. Most of that is better manufacturing and brutal competition. But once margins on the hardware hit zero, the cost moved to you.

In Q3 2024, Vizio lost $6.7M selling TVs and made $115.8M in gross profit from ads and viewing data [3]. They've said on earnings calls that they keep TV prices low to grow the audience they sell to advertisers. Walmart bought them in 2024.

This isn't a conspiracy theory either. Vizio paid $2.2M to the FTC in 2017 for tracking 11 million TVs without consent. Last December, Texas sued Samsung, LG, Sony, Hisense and TCL over ACR. Samsung and LG have since agreed to stop collecting that data without explicit consent [4].

TL;DR
1. ACR off
2. Ads + voice off
3. Smart devices on their own network
4. NextDNS filtering on the router

Sources:
[1] ACR study: http://arxiv.org/abs/2409.06203
[2] Cost of US consumer goods: http://aei.org/economics/chart-of-the-day-or-century-8
[3] Vizio Q3 2024: http://sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1835591/000183559124000088/exhibit991-q32024.htm
[4] Texas v. Samsung: http://texasattorneygeneral.gov/news/releases/attorney-general-paxton-secures-major-agreement-samsung-ensure-texans-are-protected-smart-tvs
